Hillary:
I met with Holbrooke today on water. Pakistani military called it their third most important strategic issue. Great
worries about India/Pakistan tension over 1960 agreement that regulates Indus River. We agreed our teams will work
together, most likely through the World Bank supporting the Abu Dhabi Dialogue, which brings together representatives
from the seven countries that share the Indus River Basin. This is the best forum we know of where India and Pakistan
can meet to discuss water issues. In the context of the shared waters memo and chart I gave you last week, this ranks as
potentially one of the most conflict prone, and one where the US should engage to get the parties to work together.
We are advancing well in developing a policy/action plan for you to announce on World Water Day on March 22.
Safe travels to Latin America, so glad you are going.
Maria
Under Secretary of State
for Democracy and Global Affairs
Department of State
2201 C St. NW Room 7261
Washington DC 20520
202- 647-6240

propositions.text: Pakistani military considers the Indus River water issue their third most important strategic concern.
India and Pakistan have significant tensions over the 1960 Indus River agreement.
The U.S. plans to facilitate cooperation between India and Pakistan on water issues.
The U.S. will likely use the World Bank and the Abu Dhabi Dialogue as platforms for engagement.
The Abu Dhabi Dialogue involves seven countries sharing the Indus River Basin.
The U.S. considers water conflicts in the Indus basin among the most conflict prone situations requiring engagement.
A U.S. policy/action plan on Indus water cooperation is being developed for announcement on World Water Day, March 22.
Maria is the Under Secretary of State for Democracy and Global Affairs at the U.S. Department of State.
Maria's contact details include Department of State address and phone number.
Maria met with Holbrooke today to discuss water issues.
The Pakistani military considers water their third most important strategic issue.
There are great worries about India/Pakistan tension regarding the 1960 agreement that regulates the Indus River.
Maria and Holbrooke agreed their teams will work together to address these water issues.
The cooperation will most likely be through the World Bank supporting the Abu Dhabi Dialogue.
The Abu Dhabi Dialogue brings together representatives from the seven countries that share the Indus River Basin.
The Abu Dhabi Dialogue is viewed as the best forum where India and Pakistan can meet to discuss water issues.
Within the context of the shared waters memo and chart given last week to Hillary, the Indus River Basin issue ranks as potentially one of the most conflict prone.
The United States should engage in this matter to get the parties to work together.
